title: Santorini, Greece
overview: Santorini (officially Thira) is the most dramatic of the Greek islands – a volcanic caldera crescent of white-cubic Cycladic villages perched on 300m cliffs above a deep blue sea. Oia's famous sunsets, black-sand volcanic beaches, outstanding local wine, and world-class seafood make it one of the Mediterranean's most iconic destinations. Expensive but breathtaking.
best_time_to_visit: May–June and September–October for warm weather (24–28°C), fewer crowds, and lower prices. July–August is peak season with intense crowds and prices. The island is nearly empty November–March.
climate: Mediterranean. Hot, dry summers (28–33°C), mild winters (12–15°C). Very little rain May–October. Meltemi winds can be strong in July–August.

attractions.name: Oia Sunset
attractions.description: Santorini's most famous experience – watching the sun set from the castle ruins at Oia. Arrive 2 hours early in summer for a spot. Blue-domed churches make for iconic photography.

attractions.name: Caldera Boat Tour
attractions.description: Full-day catamaran or sailing tour of the caldera visiting the volcanic hot springs, the Red Beach, and anchoring for swimming and sunset. Includes lunch and drinks.

attractions.name: Akrotiri Archaeological Site
attractions.description: Minoan Bronze Age city preserved under volcanic ash like a Greek Pompeii. One of the most important prehistoric sites in Europe. Underrated and excellent.

attractions.name: Red Beach & Perissa Black Sand Beach
attractions.description: Santorini's volcanic heritage creates unique red-cliffed and black-sand beaches. Red Beach requires a 10-min cliff walk. Perissa has sunbeds, bars, and watersports.

attractions.name: Fira Town & Caldera Walk
attractions.description: The capital town with cliffside boutiques, restaurants, and museums. Walk the 10km caldera trail from Fira to Oia for the best views on the island.

attractions.name: Santorini Wine Tasting
attractions.description: The island's volcanic soil produces exceptional Assyrtiko white wine. Santo Wines and Venetsanos Winery both have caldera-view tasting terraces.

attractions.name: Pyrgos Village
attractions.description: Medieval hilltop village with Byzantine castle ruins and far fewer tourists than Oia. The best viewpoint on the island with 360° views at sunset.

food.name: Fresh Seafood at Amoudi Bay
food.description: The small port below Oia has excellent seafood tavernas serving grilled octopus, sea urchin, and fresh-caught fish. Worth the 300-step descent.

food.name: Fava Bean Purée
food.description: Santorini's famous yellow split-pea purée is a local staple, drizzled with olive oil and capers. Perfect mezze starter at any taverna.

food.name: Tomatokeftedes (Tomato Fritters)
food.description: Local speciality made with Santorini's famous small, sweet cherry tomatoes. Crispy, delicious, and unique to the island.

food.name: Argo Restaurant (Fira)
food.description: Caldera-view restaurant with excellent modern Greek cuisine. Romantic dinner setting above the volcanic cliffs.

food.name: Breakfast with a View
food.description: Many hotels serve breakfast on caldera-view terraces. Even simple hotels in Fira offer this. One of the world's great breakfast settings.

transport: ATVs ($20-25/day) and scooters are the most popular way to explore. Car rental is also easy (~$40/day). Public buses connect main towns every 30-60 min. Water taxis connect Amoudi Bay to Fira and other points. Ferry from Athens Piraeus takes 7-9 hours; high-speed ferry 5 hours.

budget_guide.notes: Santorini is one of Greece's most expensive islands. Caldera-view hotels command a significant premium – staying in Perissa or Kamari cuts accommodation costs by 50-70% while still having great beaches.

tips: Book Oia accommodation 6+ months in advance for summer visits.
Avoid the cruise ship crowds (9am-6pm) – sightsee early morning or evening.
The caldera path from Fira to Oia is one of the world's best coastal walks – allow 4-5 hours.
Donkey rides up from the old port are controversial – the cable car is faster and kinder to animals.
Santorini wines are exceptional and unique – Assyrtiko is the signature grape.
